$comment: Sentence-level evidence map for GitHub issue #37, rebuilt against petclinic-pr@test-pr (753f724c). The issue body itself is byte-identical to the one the previous implementation (PR #48) was reviewed against — same author, same createdAt — so this skeleton reuses PR #48's block structure verbatim; only coverage/gap/tests were recomputed against this branch's own tests. Sentence text is VERBATIM from `gh issue view 37 --json body`; `sep` is the whitespace that followed it in the original.
$comment2: Per-link `strength` is `asserted` when the sentence's fact is in that test's own assertions, `exercised` when the test necessarily runs through it without checking it. A sentence with no evidence is left with tests:[] deliberately.
$comment3: Blocks mirror the issue's markdown skeleton: `p`, `hr`, `h2`, `ol`. Reconstruction is `"".join(text + sep)` per paragraph/list item, `"## " + text` per heading, `"N. " + ...` per list item, one blank line between blocks — verified below against the live issue body.

categories.$derivation: First authority is which surface catalogue the id appears in (rest.json/cucumber.json -> api, frontend.json/security.json -> unit, browser.json -> e2e).

e2e.label: e2e
e2e.blurb: drives the real UI end to end - Playwright, against the running stack.

api.label: API
api.blurb: exercises the contract under the UI — Spring MockMvc REST tests and the full-stack Cucumber/RestAssured suite.

unit.label: unit
unit.blurb: an isolated component — Spring Security config tests and Angular Karma component specs.

sentences.text: The Visit should be linked to the vet that attended that consultation.
sentences.gap: Nothing tests what happens to the link when the vet itself is deleted — the FK is ON DELETE SET NULL (AGENTS.md), a real case (a vet retiring) that no test on this branch exercises.

tests.why: POST with a vetId returns 201 and the persisted visit's vet is that vet.
Booking through /api/owners/{id}/pets/{id}/visits also records the vet, not just the flat /api/visits path.
POST with an unknown vetId is rejected with 404 — a visit can only ever link to a vet that really exists.
GET /api/visits returns vetId/vetFirstName/vetLastName for an attended visit.
The New Visit form forwards the chosen vetId to VisitService.addVisit.
A vet picked in the browser is on the visit's row afterwards - the link survives the whole round trip, not just the mapper.
The Gherkin account of the same round trip: a vet picked in the browser is on the visit afterwards.

sentences.text: Visit should display its vet everywhere throughout the app.
sentences.gap: The MCP surface still shows no vet at all: create_visit has no vetId parameter, and there is no list_visits tool to read one back. visit-list.component.spec.ts is still untouched, so the owner's page is proven only by the browser test - nothing fails fast when that column breaks.

tests.why: Deep comparison of every rendered row's .visit-vet cell against the API, vet name included.
The owner's page visit list shows the vet, checked in a real browser - the screen whose own spec file this branch never touched.
"Everywhere" is what this one is for: it follows the booking off the owner's page to /visits and finds the same vet named there.

sentences.text: **Booking a visit lets you choose the vet, and lets you not choose one.**
sentences.gap: No test asserts the field is not marked required on the form - only that omitting it books the visit anyway, through the API and through the browser.

tests.why: POST with no vetId still succeeds (201) and leaves the visit unassigned.
POST with a vetId, 201 Created, vet persisted on the visit.
Booking under the owner endpoint with a vetId also succeeds and records it.
vetOptions is the full roster, mapped to id + full name, ready to pick from.
Picking a vet and submitting forwards that vetId to the service.
An owner-admin can GET /api/vets — the precondition for the picker having anything to offer in a real deployment — but the test only checks the endpoint answers, not that the form uses it.
"Lets you choose": the picker is filled from the running stack's roster, and the vet chosen from it comes back on the visit.
"Lets you not choose one": the same form submitted without touching the picker books the visit anyway.

sentences.text: The vet is optional: half the time the appointment is booked before anyone knows who is taking it, and forcing a choice there produces bad data rather than information.
sentences.gap: Optionality is proven at creation only — nothing shows a visit may still be left vet-less later in its life, after other edits.

tests.why: POST /api/visits with no vetId, 201 Created, visit persisted with a null vet.
Booking through the form with the picker left alone succeeds, and the visit reads as unattended afterwards.

sentences.text: **Editing a visit can change the vet, and can remove it.**
sentences.gap: 6aac04b4 dropped the two tests that proved the 'remove it' half — update_withoutVet_clearsTheOneOnFile and the edit form's 'should send a null vet when the field was cleared' — deliberately, to leave that half unproven. What is left only shows a vet being changed to another vet, never cleared. Nor does anything drive the actual combo in the DOM: the surviving tests start from a payload already built in code, not a click on “-- none --” in the browser.

tests.why: PUT with a vetId assigns/changes the attending vet, verified against the database.
Renaming a visit (an edit that never touches the vet) leaves the previously attended vet exactly as it was.
The edit form's vetOptions also offers the full roster, so an existing vet can be changed to another.

sentences.text: Clearing the field must persist as empty.
sentences.gap: Both tests that ever asserted this — VisitTest.update_withoutVet_clearsTheOneOnFile (API, PUT vetId:null) and visit-edit.component.spec.ts's 'should send a null vet when the field was cleared' (unit) — were removed in 6aac04b4, on purpose, to show this requirement unproven. Nothing on the branch now asserts that a cleared vet persists as empty; the code path is unverified, not merely weakly verified.

sentences.text: We had this with pet types: the old value kept coming back.
**Wherever a visit is shown with its details, the vet is shown too.**
sentences.gap: visit-list.component.spec.ts is untouched by this branch, so the owner's page column is held up by one end-to-end test and no unit test. The same component also renders under "Previous Visits" on the New Visit screen, which nothing looks at.

tests.why: Every rendered row's .visit-vet cell matches the API's vet name, or 'none'.
The vet reaches the owner's page, from outside the app - the surface the Karma specs do not cover.

sentences.text: Today that means the owner's page and the all-visits screen.
sentences.gap: Both screens the sentence names now have a test, but by different routes: the all-visits screen at component level, the owner's page only end to end.

tests.why: All-visits screen: every row's vet cell checked.
The owner's page half of the pair, in a browser; visits-page.component.spec covers the all-visits half.

sentences.text: **A visit with no vet reads as having none.**
sentences.gap: vetLabel() itself still has no standalone unit test - its coverage is incidental, through the two screens that call it.

tests.why: The vet-less 2025 visit renders the exact text 'none' in its .visit-vet cell.
A visit booked with no vet reads exactly "none" on the owner's page - the screen where vetLabel() had no coverage at all.
The Gherkin account of the same claim: booking with the vet picker untouched leaves the visit's row on the owner's page reading "none".

sentences.text: Not "Unknown", not blank-because-broken, and never an error.
sentences.gap: 'Never an error' is proven only by absence - no test deliberately forces an error path (a malformed vet reference already on a row, say) to check the cell still renders instead of breaking.

tests.why: Exact-text match on 'none' excludes both 'Unknown' and a blank cell.
toHaveText is an exact match, so "Unknown", a blank cell and a rendering error would each fail it.
A dedicated scenario for the negative case, read in a browser: the row states "none" rather than leaving a blank or erroring cell.

sentences.text: Visits created before this change have no vet and will not get one.
sentences.gap: The visit it checks is created fresh inside the test itself, not a genuinely pre-migration row — it never distinguishes 'never had a vet' from 'predates the vet_id column', and 'will not get one' remains a non-event no test can prove.

tests.why: Reads back a freshly created vet-less visit and finds vetId/vetFirstName/vetLastName all null, without singling out pre-existing rows.

sentences.text: Searching or filtering visits by vet.

uncolouredRationale.s7: A reference to an older defect in pet types. It is a note about the ticket's own history, not a claim about this system.
uncolouredRationale.s13: A scope exclusion. No test proves the absence of a feature.

$branchNotes: 6aac04b4 removed VisitTest.update_withoutVet_clearsTheOneOnFile and visit-edit.component.spec.ts's 'should send a null vet when the field was cleared' — on purpose, per its own commit message, to leave 'clearing the field must persist as empty' (s6) unproven. s5 downgrades from covered to partly (only the 'change' half survives); s6 drops from covered to missing. getAll_namesTheVetAndLeavesUnattendedVisitsEmpty (s1, s2, s12) and findVisitsByPetId shifted from :338/:373 to :318/:353 in the same file, with no change in substance.

The test-changes manifest (test-changes-new.json) flags 5 tests as 'modified': VisitTest.update_ok, BasicAuthenticationConfigTest.adminUser_canAccessOwners, the 'Edit a visit description' scenario, and both components' 'should navigate to owner detail via gotoOwnerDetail' specs. Diffing each against origin/main shows all five are byte-identical — they only shifted line numbers because new tests were inserted above them in the same files. Recorded here as unchanged in substance.

The branch shipped without any Playwright/browser test of the vet: the three commits under review touch nothing in petclinic-test/, although the generated diagram petclinic-test/generated/add-visit.spec.ts.add-a-visit-attended-by-a-vet.genseq.puml was still on the branch, titled with a link to a scenario that no longer existed. Two scenarios in add-visit.spec.ts now carry that evidence (see browser.json); every other sentence still rests on backend MockMvc/Cucumber tests and Angular Karma component specs.

visit-list.component (the owner's-page / 'Previous Visits' visit table) gained the same Vet column and vetLabel() call as the all-visits screen, but visit-list.component.spec.ts was not touched — nothing on this branch tests it.
